weekly.method: Analyst judgments on the existing 1–5 broad-risk-support scale. Arithmetic mean of five factors; no new numeric regime thresholds. These scores are INFERENCES, not measured probabilities or strategy validation.

factors.name: Growth
factors.facts: Q3 real GDP +3.4% annualized and private domestic final demand +4.9% (BEA, Oct 29). October payrolls +165,000, unemployment 4.1%, and prior payroll revisions +84,000 (BLS, Nov 6).
factors.meaning: Expansion is resilient enough to support broad risk in isolation.
factors.counterevidence: September real consumption was nearly flat and real disposable income fell 0.3%; strong quarterly activity does not guarantee near-term acceleration.

factors.name: Inflation
factors.facts: September PCE inflation was 3.6% year over year; core 3.1%. Monthly increases were 0.5% and 0.3% (BEA, Oct 29).
factors.meaning: Inflation remains a policy constraint and a headwind to broad risk.
factors.counterevidence: Quarterly PCE inflation slowed in Q3. Elevated monthly inflation is not proof that every underlying component is accelerating.

factors.name: Rates
factors.facts: The Oct 28 Fed decision held the target at 3.75–4.00%; two dissents favored a hike. The 10Y real yield was 2.60% on Nov 5, down 4 bp from Nov 4.
factors.meaning: Real discount rates remain a burden despite marginal relief. Falling yields do not alone establish a risk-on trade.
factors.counterevidence: Lower real yields offer relief; no verified current futures-implied policy path is available.

factors.name: Credit
factors.facts: On Nov 5, HY OAS widened 16 bp to 348 bp and IG OAS widened 2 bp to 93 bp versus Nov 4.
factors.meaning: Financing conditions deteriorated in both credit tiers on the latest common day; this weakens equity risk confirmation.
factors.counterevidence: IG OAS was 94 bp on Oct 30. One-day deterioration does not establish a systemic credit crisis; issuance and bank lending are not refreshed.

factors.name: Liquidity
factors.facts: Week ended Nov 4: reserves rose $36.318bn and TGA fell $42.552bn versus Oct 28. Fed assets rose $2.510bn. Nov 5 SOFR 3.92% versus IORB 3.90%.
factors.meaning: Plumbing improved on these measures, but the evidence supports a balanced assessment rather than a broad liquidity-driven rally.
factors.counterevidence: NFCI rose to -0.459 from -0.467 for Oct 30 (less loose). Repo/funding observations are proxies; collateral and cross-currency stress are unmeasured.

weekly.lead_driver: Inflation and restrictive discount rates constrain a resilient expansion; recent credit and equity weakness add a defensive market overlay. Causal dominance is unconfirmed.
weekly.failure1: Inflation cools while real yields ease, credit stabilizes and broad earnings/price participation improves: restrictive-transition assessment loses support.
weekly.failure2: Labor and real demand weaken alongside sustained HY/IG widening and funding deterioration: mixed expansion gives way to a more defensive growth regime.

weekly.review_note: Reviewed Nov 7 after automatic collection: IORB observation advanced to Nov 7 at the unchanged 3.90% rate. Other accepted latest observations were unchanged. Scores and regime retained. Three series retained their later dated snapshots when the first automatic responses were older; this limits refresh coverage.
